dedupe_keys.name: hqsc health system quality dashboard and atlas of healthcare variation new zealand quality safety and service use indicators by district

description: These two products from New Zealand's health quality agency show how the quality, safety and use of health care vary across the country's health districts and population groups. They are published by the Health Quality & Safety Commission Te Tāhū Hauora, which develops the indicators with clinicians and subject-matter experts. The dashboard of health system quality brings measures across domains together with equity views, a Māori health equity report and national quality priorities, while the Atlas of Healthcare Variation presents clinician-agreed indicators for domains such as diabetes, asthma, gout, opioids, polypharmacy and surgical procedures by age, gender, ethnicity, district, rural or urban living and, for some domains, primary health organisation. Both are free and available on the web, the dashboard through Tableau and the Atlas as interactive domain pages with supporting documents; there is no bulk download. Caveats: the Atlas shows variation without judging which level is right and should not be used to rank areas, and domains are updated on different cycles. Simulation uses: parameterising regional differences in service use and quality for health system capacity and equity models. Related records: the NMDS hospital events (data-nz-nmds-hospital-events) are the main source for hospital indicators, and the AIHW MyHospitals API (data-aihw-myhospitals-api) is a comparable Australian product.
